subject: MAP: Technical evaluation plan (Acme) - draft & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sophie Lee <sophie.lee@acme.com>; Tom Harrison <tom.harrison@acme.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 1 Aug 2027 14:10:00 -0700
Subject: MAP: Technical evaluation plan (Acme) - draft & next steps

Thanks for the time today — great discussion. As promised, attaching an updated MAP draft focused on the Technical Evaluation milestone. High level summary and asks below.

Quick recap / context:
- Goal: validate Redwood can meet Acme's latency, cost, and quality targets for the customer-facing summarization flow before pilot sign-off.
- Success = meet benchmark thresholds (see below) + pass qualitative review on representative prompt set.

Attached: acme-map-draft-v2.pdf (MAP draft) and technical-eval-checklist.xlsx (detailed steps).

Technical evaluation milestone (proposed):
1) Benchmark preparation (owner: Acme/Redwood) — target complete by 2027-08-10
   - Deliverables: sample eval dataset (200 prompts + expected outputs), load profile, representative prompt metadata (avg/95th tokens)
   - Responsible: Acme (provide data), Redwood (provide perf harness)

2) Performance & cost benchmarking (owner: Redwood) — target complete by 2027-08-14
   - Perf targets (P95 latency measured from API): < 180 ms for 1k-token request pattern (typical summarization request profile)
   - Throughput target: sustain 200 reqs/sec for 30s burst without QoS degradation
   - Cost target: end-to-end inference cost <= $0.50 per 1k output tokens (config-dependent; includes batching/quantization savings)
   - Deliverables: perf report (latency percentiles, GPU utilization, ops/sec), cost estimate by config

3) Quality evaluation (owner: Acme/Redwood) — target complete by 2027-08-16
   - Success criteria: >= 90% pass rate on automated metrics and human review on a 200-item eval set
   - Model shortlist: Llama-3-Chat-8B (q4_0), Mistral-Instruct-7B (8-bit), Falcon-40B-Instruct (int8/quantized)
   - Deliverables: quality report, example failure cases, recommended model/config

4) Security & compliance check (owner: Acme/Redwood) — target complete by 2027-08-18
   - Ensure no PII exfiltration in sampled outputs, verify audit logging and retention config on Redwood Dedicated/Private as applicable

5) MAP sign-off (owner: Acme/Redwood) — target close date: 2027-08-20

Open items / asks for Acme:
- Please share the representative eval dataset (200 prompts) and one representative high-frequency prompt pattern by 2027-08-05
- Confirm whether test runs must be executed inside Acme VPC or if public-hosted endpoints are OK for the initial perf pass

Internal notes for Redwood:
- Camila: we'll provide the perf harness and an initial config matrix (batch sizes, kv cache settings, quant profiles)
- Dylan: please prepare two instance configs for benchmarking (A100:p4d-style and 8xA10G equivalent) and estimate concurrency limits

Next steps:
- Sophie/Raj: confirm dataset delivery timeline and VPC requirement by EOD 2027-08-03
- We'll run the first perf pass once sample data is received and share results within 48 hours

Thanks — looking forward to the next steps.

—
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0192

Attachments: acme-map-draft-v2.pdf, technical-eval-checklist.xlsx
From: Sophie Lee <sophie.lee@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Tom Harrison <tom.harrison@acme.com>, Raj Patel <raj.patel@acme.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Aug 2027 09:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP: Technical evaluation plan (Acme) - draft & next steps

Thanks Marissa — appreciate the clear plan. A few quick clarifications after syncing with Tom and Raj: 

On the dataset: we can deliver the 200 prompt eval set, but Raj asked whether you need any label formats (CSV w/ id, prompt, expected_output) or a different structure. We'll aim to deliver by 8/10 but can try for 8/05 if format is straightforward.

On environment: for initial perf passes we prefer Redwood to run against a staging endpoint (public) so we can iterate faster. If perf looks good we will require a follow-up run in our VPC for final verification. Is that workflow OK?

On timelines: given internal review cycles on our side, can we move the MAP sign-off target to 2027-08-20 instead of 8/16? That gives us time for a second pass after the VPC run.

Also looping in Raj (our infra lead) — Raj, can you confirm whether you need any firewall/IP allowlists or a VPN for the initial staging run?

On the shortlist you proposed — Tom had a question about Falcon-40B costs in your estimate. Can Camila share a ballpark cost delta between Falcon-40B-instruct quantized vs Llama-3-Chat-8B q4 for the same throughput?

On quoting: we will likely need a short SOW addendum if we hit the VPC verification step; Tom can own that procurement thread.

Thanks,
Sophie

From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Aug 2027 13:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP: Technical evaluation plan (Acme) - draft & next steps

Hi all — quick answers from the engineering side and what we'll provide.

1) Dataset format: CSV with columns [id, prompt, expected_output, metadata(json)] works fine. If you have labels in a different format we can ingest a JSONL as well. Please include tokenization hints if possible.

2) Perf harness: Redwood will provide a reproducible benchmark harness (JMeter wrapper + Python runner) and a one-click script to upload the eval set. Link to instructions: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-acme-eval (see perf-harness-instructions.md attached). We'll also provide pre-built containers if you prefer to run within your VPC.

3) Cost delta (ballpark): for the same throughput and latency envelope we expect:
   - Llama-3-Chat-8B (q4_0) ~ baseline cost X
   - Mistral-Instruct-7B (8-bit) ~ -15% vs baseline for throughput heavy workloads
   - Falcon-40B-Instruct (int8) ~ +30-50% cost vs 8B-class due to larger model size, though quantization reduces this a lot.
Exact numbers depend on batching and sequence length — we'll include a per-config cost table in the perf report.

4) IP allowlist: if you're running the staging endpoint, we'll give you the public IP ranges to allow. For VPC runs we'll coordinate a short VPN handoff. Raj — I'll follow up separately with an allowlist and container artifacts.

5) Deliverables we'll upload to the drive folder once benchmark runs complete: perf_report.pdf, cost_estimate.csv, quality_report.md.

Attaching: technical-eval-checklist.xlsx and perf-harness-instructions.md

Camila
Staff Software Engineer, Performance
camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com
